# rustclipsync-core

English · [简体中文](README-ZH.md)

The shared Rust core for RustClipSync clients, extracted from the Omaclipsync 0.2.0 synchronization implementation. Linux and Windows clients reuse its message state machine and HTTPS protocol with platform-specific adapters. This is a client library, not a server or a standalone desktop application.

## Current API

All network operations use `/api/...` and require wire protocol **3**. This release deliberately rejects older servers and clients: deploy matching versions together, or keep old clients on the previous server. Device credentials and the encrypted-state format remain unchanged. Rust desktop clients and Omaclipsync consume exported snapshots of this repository; endpoint logic must be changed here and re-exported.

## Components

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `client` / `transport` | HTTPS registration and data, persistent WSS direction control with HTTP fallback, cancellation, acknowledgment and long polling; the transport interface supports offline tests |
| `state` | UUID, epoch, revision, outbox, receive cursor and apply journal; compatible with the existing RCS1 AES-256-GCM state format |
| `session` | Latest-only offline synchronization, retries with a stable message ID, conflict handling, sensitive-content settings, pre-apply checks and loop suppression |
| `worker` | Metadata long polling, notification coalescing and connection backoff; clipboard text is not copied to the polling thread |
| `Filter` | Regex filters for uploads and downloads |
| `adapters` | Interfaces for system clipboard access, atomic state storage and optional history |

The library has no Wayland, WinUI, Windows API, Secret Service, tray or file-path dependencies. Creating a session loads or creates encrypted state but does not connect to the network or read or write the clipboard. Hosts must serialize synchronization calls on a dedicated worker thread; do not perform blocking network operations on the UI thread.

The current library version, `0.4.0`, identifies the shared Rust API independently of server and client product versions. The `/api/` prefix identifies the current HTTP API without a version in its path; `X-RCS-Protocol: 3` negotiates the required protocol.

## Adapter responsibilities

1. Obtain a random 32-byte key from the platform credential store: Secret Service on Linux or DPAPI CurrentUser on Windows.
2. Implement `StateStore` with bounded reads, access restricted to the current user and atomic replacement; persist all bytes generated by the core. Return `None` only when the file does not exist. Never silently recreate the identity after decryption fails.
3. Implement `Clipboard` to return text and sensitivity markers and attach a source marker to writes. A successful `write` means the system clipboard accepted the content; storing it only in a private inbox must not be reported as `applied`.
4. Use `NoHistory` or implement `HistorySink`. The core neither dictates a history storage format nor logs clipboard text.
5. Create a session with `SessionConfig` and `Session::open`. Call `set_sync_direction(SyncDirection::Bidirectional, false)` (or the selected direction/pause state) before `check`; the default unknown direction denies data. The watcher maintains a shared local event counter; record real events with `record_local` / `record_clear` and synchronize using `flush` / `pull`.

On a state persistence error, pause and rebuild the session instead of continuing with in-memory state that may be ahead of disk. On first startup, do not mistake existing clipboard content for a new copy event. Notifications are wake-up signals; the epoch and revision returned by `state` determine synchronization.

Synchronization entry points check restored pending content against the current clipboard before sending. `flush` applies the current sensitive-content and regex policies to the latest queued value. An oversized new copy also supersedes the old value; uncertain uploads are resolved through cancellation before they are discarded. If a clipboard write returns an error, the session durably records it as `skipped` before returning the error, so later receives can continue without replaying the ambiguous write. A failure to save that recovery is a state persistence error and requires rebuilding the session.

`Error`, `SyncError` and `ClipboardError` implement `Display` and `std::error::Error`. Their display text omits underlying URLs and adapter-provided details; `source()` retains the typed causes for callers that need to inspect them. `Worker::shutdown()` requests a stop without waiting. `Worker::join()` requests a stop and waits for completion, returning any thread panic to the host; call it away from the UI thread. Dropping a worker still requests a stop without waiting. Custom `Transport` implementations must bound each operation, including the entire long-poll request, with a finite timeout; shutdown cannot interrupt an in-flight custom call.

## Protocol and privacy constraints

- Connects to the [RustClipSync server](https://github.com/Infinifar/rustclipsync-server) using its [protocol](https://github.com/Infinifar/rustclipsync-server/blob/main/PROTOCOL.md). Legacy SyncClipboard HTTP/SignalR transport is not implemented.
- A UUID identifies one copy event and remains stable across retries. Revisions determine order; epochs separate server resets. Client time is used only for retry expiry, not ordering or uniqueness.
- Automatic uploads do not silently overwrite conflicts; offline synchronization keeps only the latest value. When an upload outcome is uncertain, retain the request and resolve or cancel it before processing a newer value.
- Persistent cursors and acknowledgments prevent replay. A message whose clipboard write outcome is unknown after a crash is recovered as `skipped`; exactly-once clipboard side effects are not guaranteed.
- The host supplies sensitive markers; synchronization should be disabled by default. Neither markers nor regular expressions can identify all sensitive information.
- TLS certificates are verified by default. Plain HTTP, credentials embedded in URLs and redirects are rejected. The explicit `insecure` option is intended only for controlled tests or self-signed environments.
- State encryption protects files at rest, not end-to-end traffic; the server can read synchronized text. Text, keys and pairing passwords in memory are not currently guaranteed to be cleared immediately.
- Text is limited to 10 MiB per item and state to 64 MiB. Long-poll worker shutdown waits for bounded direction negotiation plus the current HTTP request's 30-second timeout; hosts must avoid repeatedly creating overlapping workers.


## Device direction and protocol 3

`direction::SyncDirection` has `PushOnly`, `ReceiveOnly` and `Bidirectional`,
serialized as `PUSH_ONLY`, `RECEIVE_ONLY`, `BIDIRECTIONAL`. Pause is a separate
boolean and retains the chosen direction. Unknown, revoked and paused states
receive no messages; receive-only and paused sessions cannot publish. The core
retains local send/receive guards even when reporting fails.

```rust,no_run
use rustclipsync_core::direction::SyncDirection;
// After Session::open, before check/flush/pull:
// session.set_sync_direction(SyncDirection::Bidirectional, false)?;
// session.check()?; // register -> direction ACK -> metadata
// session.set_sync_direction(SyncDirection::ReceiveOnly, false)?;
// session.set_sync_direction(SyncDirection::ReceiveOnly, true)?; // pause
// session.revoke_sync_direction()?; // explicit logout, not ordinary shutdown
```

The host must increment its local event generation before changing direction,
pausing or logging out, stop its old notification worker, and serialize session
calls on its background thread. A failed update retains the **new local policy**
and reports an error; a failed logout is **unconfirmed**, never a successful
revocation. Ordinary `Worker::shutdown`, process close or network loss does not
revoke direction, preserving offline backfill. Explicit re-pairing uses
`re_pair_with_direction(direction, paused)`; failed old-session revocation does
not destroy the old identity.

The HTTPS client keeps one bounded control WebSocket at `/api/ws`, authenticates
with Bearer and the protocol header (never tokens in URLs), and sends tagged
`SyncDirectionUpdate` / `SyncDirectionRevoke` frames. It validates the matching
`SyncDirectionAck` device/session/version. WS connection or I/O failure retries
**the identical operation** through HTTP, preserving idempotency when a WS ACK
was lost. A failed HTTP retry remains pending. Direction control uses a separate
mutex; the lock is not held across the HTTP long poll. The poll is capped at
30 seconds; an initial discovery/control/fallback can add up to 40 seconds, so
worker shutdown must remain off the UI thread. WebSocket frames are
limited to 4096 bytes with a 10-second I/O deadline, including slow fragments. HTTPS discovery supplies the resolved peer address,
avoiding an additional unbounded system DNS lookup. With an HTTP proxy that
cannot carry the control socket, the same authenticated HTTP fallback is used.

HTTP fallback and state discovery use:

- `GET /api/devices/{deviceId}/sync-direction`: read the current version without
  activating state or refreshing TTL.
- `PUT` at that path: `{sessionId, version, direction, paused, connect}`. A fresh
  canonical UUID and `connect:true` claim a session via GET then CAS=current+1;
  ordinary updates use the current session and `connect:false`.
- `DELETE` at that path: `{sessionId, version}`. Logout retains a versioned
  tombstone; an exact retry is idempotent. Delayed old updates cannot revive it.

Example update (the WebSocket variant adds `type: "SyncDirectionUpdate"`):

```json
{"sessionId":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","version":1,"direction":"BIDIRECTIONAL","paused":false,"connect":true}
```

Every sync response must advertise `X-RCS-Protocol: 3`. HTTP 426 with
`PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED` is terminal, including an older peer that omits the
header. Structured errors also distinguish `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `DEVICE_MISMATCH`,
`VERSION_STALE`, `SESSION_REVOKED`, `SESSION_OFFLINE`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `INVALID_DIRECTION` and
`DIRECTION_FORBIDDEN`. Fenced sessions stop old workers; they do not silently
claim another session to replay stale settings. An explicit host connection or
policy update starts a new attempt. `SESSION_OFFLINE` means only the current
session lease expired; the core reconnects with fresh GET+CAS without blindly
retrying the old data request. Errors from an older in-flight session cannot
reset or fence a newer accepted session. Data requests carry the accepted
`X-RCS-Sync-Session`; registration, direction control and cancellation do not.

A reconnect reports the latest direction and waits for ACK before reading data.
The server can replay **at most one eligible message per device** from its
administrator-configured window. The client does not contain a backfill-window
constant or fetch the global current message as a fallback. Window values and
zero/expiry semantics belong to the [server configuration](https://github.com/Infinifar/rustclipsync-server/blob/main/docs/DIRECTION-PROTOCOL.md).
Direction TTL is server-owned: valid reporting/login/activity refreshes it;
30-day inactivity revokes eligibility and requires a new report.

`RemoteState.revision` remains the global upload-conflict revision, while nullable
`deliveryRevision` identifies an authorized per-device message. The notification
worker keeps a separate monotonic observed-global cursor so filtered metadata
does not cause a hot polling loop; host updates cannot roll that cursor back. A valid delivery
older than the global revision is processed before advancing the local cursor.
An absent delivery may advance observation, but never rebases a queued upload.
Bodies require current direction/session authorization on the server. The
existing durable apply journal, skipped acknowledgements, sensitive inbox,
local generation checks and explicit conflict policy remain in effect.

Custom `Transport` implementations must implement `set_sync_direction`,
`ensure_sync_direction` and `revoke_sync_direction`, in addition to the existing
HTTP operations. The new public methods/types and `RemoteState.delivery_revision`
are a Rust API break represented by crate 0.4.0.

## Development and consumption

```bash
cargo test --locked
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

With a server test binary available, run the HTTPS protocol integration test:

```bash
python3 tests/server_e2e.py ../rustclipsync-server/target/release/rustclipsync-server
```

This requires Python 3 and OpenSSL. It launches a temporary server, database and loopback-only HTTPS proxy, using in-memory clipboard and key-store substitutes without touching the user's desktop. Unit tests include an encrypted state migration fixture generated by unmodified Omaclipsync 0.2.0 code. See [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md) for scope and platform limitations.

For local development with adjacent repositories:

```toml
rustclipsync-core = { version = "=0.4.0", path = "../rustclipsync-core" }
```

The [source repository](https://github.com/Infinifar/rustclipsync-core) is public under the MIT license and is not published on crates.io. To keep standalone Omaclipsync checkouts and source packages buildable, Omaclipsync consumes an automatically exported snapshot in `core/vendor/rustclipsync-core`:

```bash
python3 tools/export_source.py ../omarchy-plugins-dev/io.github.infinifar.omaclipsync/core/vendor/rustclipsync-core
python3 tools/export_source.py ../omarchy-plugins-dev/io.github.infinifar.omaclipsync/core/vendor/rustclipsync-core --check
```

The export manifest records the source version, original extraction commit and SHA-256 of each file. Do not edit consumer snapshots directly: change this repository, run tests, re-export, then update the consumer's Cargo.lock. A future library release can move consumers to a pinned version or Git commit instead of a floating branch.

The Windows and Linux desktop client is [RustClipSync Desktop](https://github.com/Infinifar/rustclipsync-desktop), with WinUI 3 on Windows 11 and a standalone Qt 6/QML interface on Linux. Linux x86_64 packages target Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 43 and Arch/Omarchy, without requiring Omarchy or Quickshell. See the [downloads](https://github.com/Infinifar/rustclipsync-desktop/releases) and [Linux guide](https://github.com/Infinifar/rustclipsync-desktop/blob/main/LINUX.md). X11 is supported; Wayland requires data-control support, and GNOME/Wayland sessions without it are currently unsupported.

The [Omaclipsync plugin](https://github.com/Infinifar/omaclipsync) provides integration with the Omarchy shell. Both desktop clients and the plugin reuse this core through platform adapters. Android currently implements the same protocol in Kotlin without JNI.

MIT license. The original implementation came from `Infinifar/omaclipsync`, extraction baseline commit `a8c330136886ad547dfadf386bb66901b3bbc45c`. New cross-platform interfaces, tests and export tools are maintained here.

## 0.2.0: private sensitive inbox

Clients can call `Session::use_sensitive_inbox(true)`. With sensitive synchronization enabled, incoming sensitive text and the receive cursor are stored in one encrypted state commit and acknowledged as `skipped`, without claiming a system clipboard write. Only the latest item is retained; `clear_inbox(id)` does not reset the cursor. Default receive behavior is unchanged. `HistorySink::record_marked` lets platforms exclude sensitive text from ordinary history; notification identity does not contain inbox text.

The new `Persisted.inbox` field defaults to empty when reading older encrypted files. The state limit is now 64 MiB to accommodate worst-case pending, replacement and private inbox items. This Rust API change was released as crate 0.2.0 without changing the server HTTP protocol.

### Clipboard-free background inbox receive

`Session::pull_inbox(observed)` receives marked sensitive messages only when the
private encrypted inbox is enabled. It reuses `pull` validation and persistence,
never accesses the clipboard, and acknowledges durable inbox storage as `skipped`.
Ordinary messages remain unconsumed for foreground `pull`; the server still only
retains its latest value. Pairing and restored outbox checks must finish in the
foreground first. Pending uploads are left for foreground resolution. Hosts own
scheduling and platform lifetime limits; this API does not grant background runtime.

`Session::pull_background(observed, true)` additionally permits clipboard writes
without reading the clipboard, subject to the existing sensitive policy. Platforms
must require a separate explicit opt-in: without a readable snapshot, another
app's recently copied value may be overwritten. Pending uploads remain deferred.
